---
title: "Accessing the Course Repository"
---

The course repository contains the website source, slides, notebooks, assets,
and a shared-library submodule. Students should treat the instructor's
repository as read-only. Coursework will not be submitted through Git.

## Prerequisites

Install Git and choose either HTTPS or SSH authentication for GitHub.

## Clone the repository

Choose one method.

### HTTPS

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/fjhickernell/MATH332Fall2026.git
cd MATH332Fall2026
```

### SSH

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:fjhickernell/MATH332Fall2026.git
cd MATH332Fall2026
```

::: {.callout-note}
The GitHub repository link will become usable after the repository is
published. Until then, these commands document the intended setup.
:::

## Verify the submodule

```bash
git submodule status
```

If `classlib` was not initialized, run:

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

## Get course updates

From the repository directory, run:

```bash
git pull --ff-only
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

The second command checks out the shared library version recorded by the
course repository. Do not use `git submodule update --remote` unless the
instructor explicitly requests it.

## If you have local changes

Check your work before updating:

```bash
git status
```

Copy important work outside the course repository or commit it to your own
private repository before pulling updates. Ask for help rather than discarding
changes you want to keep.
